authors: Raj Pathak, Neil Turner, Leila Alinaghian
method: systematic literature review (4,536->81 papers; Gioia method)
definition: Turner (2006): governance 'provides the structure through which the objectives of the project are set, the means of attaining those objectives... and the means of monitoring performance are determined'; APM (2019, p. 212): 'the framework of authority and accountability that defines and controls outputs, outcomes and benefits.'
elements: mechanisms (formal: alliance, process/institutional framework, contract, assurance/governmental, goal-alignment; informal: network, trust, relationship mgmt)
stakeholders: Multi-party; owner/client, governments, contractors, suppliers; 'no actor has total control and authority over all others' (von Danwitz).
temporality_detail: Moderate. Governance 'is regarded as dynamic, processual and anchored in multiple levels' (Abstract); evolutionary governance - 'governance issues as being static, but project development processes and environments are dynamic... governance regimes must adapt... and change as the project development process unfolds' (p. 9). No electoral cycle.
megaproject_detail: Systematic review of megaproject governance; inter-org core.
misalignment_detail: Names multi-level & evolutionary governance and future-research topics (governance at different levels; IPD (mis)alignment) - but no electoral/temporal-misalignment agenda.
gaps: Field-level confirmation of multi-level + evolutionary governance; no electoral-temporal agenda named.
key_quotes: Governance 'is regarded as dynamic, processual and anchored in multiple levels' (Abstract).
'governance regimes must adapt... and change as the project development process unfolds' (Miller & Hobbs, via p. 9).
coding_notes: Cites items 5, 6, 12, 13, 15 in this corpus - a citation hub. Neil Turner distinct from Rodney Turner (item 14).
